newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Indian team arrives for peace talks with Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Indian team arrives for peace talks with Pakistan.

text.p: Indian negotiators arrived in Islamabad on Thursday for a second round of peace talks that they said would focus on the methodology for future talks between the two old enemies.
But the Pakistani side made it clear it would try to focus on what it regards the "core issue" of the dispute between the two countries over the Himalayan region of Jammu and Kashmir.
"Our immediate task is to...focus on the modalities, methodology and structure of dialogue," Indian Foreign Ministry secretary Salman Haider told reporters at Islamabad airport.

Haider, leading a six-member delegation, will meet his Pakistani counterpart Shamshasd Ahmad on Friday afternoon at the start of a four-day second round of the talks, which follow their first round in New Delhi in March.
"The agenda is to continue our discussions of which we already had one round in Delhi," the top Indian diplomat said.
However, Ahmad told reporters that Kashmir dispute "lies at the heart of all problems that affect our region".
"So naturally, it is our earnest desire, and it will be our endeavour to focus on this issue as part of our overall attempt to find a peaceful solution of all problems that face us."

Haider said New Delhi shared the desire with Islamabad to seek good neighbourly relations between the two countries, which have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over Kashmir.

Earlier on Thursday, Prime Ministers Inder Kumar Gujral of India and Nawaz Sharif of Pakistan spoke for the first time on a telephone "hotline" set up to help dispel mistrust between the two long-time foes.
Gujral and Sharif had agreed to set up the direct phone link between their two offices when they met for the first time in the Maldives last month on the margins of a regional summit.

Ahmad and Haider met in New Delhi in March to restart bilateral talks which had become bogged down in 1994 in disagreement over Kashmir, two-thirds of which is ruled by India and the rest by Pakistan.

Ahmad met Kashmiri political leaders living on the Pakistani side and assured them of Islamabad's "continued moral, political and diplomatic support" in what Pakistan calls Kashmiris' struggle for their right to self-determination.
The official APP news agency quoted Ahmad as telling them that "a determined effort will be made to address all outstanding issues, including the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir".
